newsitem.title: UK: Prince Charles' love will not wed him, paper says.
newsitem.headline: Prince Charles' love will not wed him, paper says.

text.p: Camilla Parker Bowles, the divorced intimate companion of Prince Charles, will not wed the heir to the British throne despite the end of his marriage to Princess Diana, the Sun newspaper said.
In its Tuesday edition, the top-selling tabloid said Camilla had come to the reluctant conclusion after a series of heart-to-heart meetings with the prince.
"I'll never wed Prince Charles," she was quoted as telling friends.
Speculation that the prince might marry his long-time love Camilla grew after Charles' divorce from Diana, his wife of 15 years, became final at the end of August.
The Sun, a newspaper with a good track record of royal exclusives, said Camilla and Charles decided they had to confront the issue after the prince's divorce.
Church leaders have warned the prince that he cannot expect to be the next king if he weds Camilla. Opinion polls show the British people share the same misgivings about a possible "Queen Camilla".
The Sun quoted a close friend of Camilla as saying: "Marriage to the Prince of Wales is not in her head and she does not want people to think that it is.
"The Church of England, politicians and the public all have strong views on a marriage and Camilla recognises that."
The Sun said, however, that Camilla, 49, and Charles, 47, were determined to continue their 20-year love affair, maintaining a discreet and long-term relationship.

Charles and Diana were divorced on August 28, and Diana made it clear that she felt herself to be the wronged party when she appeared in public that day still wearing her engagement and wedding rings.
Ingrid Seward, a prominent royal commentator, said Camilla "cannot face the aggravation of being an official member of the royal family".
"She realises it would probably cost the man she loves his inheritance were he to make her his wife," Seward said.
She added: "The prince has reluctantly come to agree with her. He knows people will not entertain Camilla as queen."

Although the former head of the Church of England, Robert Runcie, has described Diana as "an actress and a schemer", many Britons remain under the spell of the glamorous princess, believing her to have been wronged by Charles, who has admitted adultery.
The Sun said Charles, who has spent a lifetime being groomed for the monarchy, had accepted he could not wed Camilla and had decided to put his duty before love.
A close friend of the couple was quoted as saying: "The prince puts his duty above all else. He sees that duty and responsibility as incompatible with marriage to Mrs Parker Bowles."
Aides to the prince were now making long-term plans to boost his popularity and to tackle what they call "the Camilla problem".
